release_note.summary: The course guides now show what individuals, nonprofits and small businesses can build today. SE 301 and SE 401 connect the planned local AI studio to sponsored hosting for member-built apps. The Change Log and signed-in updates explain releases in plain language, and the course and funding sections are easier to read on smaller screens.
release_note.technical_summary: All four change-log views retain their navigation order and expose their active page. Agent metadata keeps the release sequence, timestamp, pull request and commit evidence alongside the reader summary.

2026-11-21: The launch moved from a course outline to sixteen AI Tips, a complete ten-lesson SE 101 sequence and a book sample. Learners could watch in place and pick up where they stopped.
2026-11-22: People gained a way to contribute stories or take a copy of the project. Their AI assistants gained Markdown guides to the same pages, while editors gained a staging site for review.
2026-11-23: SE 201 connected its design and operating lessons with a worked feature. Learners could follow the decisions from the opening plan through verification.
2026-11-24: A complete course and a clearer editorial record
The final SE 201 recording completed the course. Video dates helped readers spot new material, while the public outline, policy and contributor credits made the book’s development easier to follow.
2026-11-25: The book acquired voices beyond its preview
Two nonfiction chapters, a guest contribution and a revised narrated preview gave readers several ways into the book. AI Tips also added a lesson on keeping secrets out of prompts.
2026-11-26: Run models locally and pick up lessons across devices

SE 301 opened its ten-lab local AI playbook, and SE 401 outlined a possible nonprofit cohort. My learning brings your profile and saved lessons together. When the account service needs time to start, you can wait or retry sign-in on the article you were reading.

2026-W47: A library people and their agents could use

The opening weekend established the learning experience. A visitor could finish SE 101, listen to a book preview and bring an assistant to read the same material. The contribution and copy paths opened the work to other builders.
2026-W48: The site became a worked example of the courses

The enterprise course finished with an end-to-end capstone, and SE 301 extended that practice to learners’ own machines. The site now exposes its own release record, so a learner can follow a change from a plain-language explanation to its source. About places the proposed nonprofit cohort alongside the material people can already use.

2026-11: An open engineering school takes shape

November brought together practical courses, the OpenBook and a contribution path for outside experience. Readers can watch a lesson, study its source or take a copy of the project. The new production archive gives them a way to check how that project evolves. About connects this work to the proposed foundation and names what a first cohort would still have to demonstrate.
